The Psi of Basaveshwaranagara Police Station has laid charge sheet against accused Nos.1 & 2 for
the offence punishable U/s.420 & 414 of Ipc.
2. The Prosecution'S Case In Nutshell Is As Under:
That, o

n 21.05.2022, at 12-15 pm., while CW-1/PW-1 was at her Dry Fruits Shop,
situated at No.222, 7 th Cross, 1st Main, Manjunathnagar 1st Phase, the accused No.1 having drawn the attention of PW-1 by requesting PW-1 to pack Dry Fruits weighing half KG each, persuaded PW-1 to handover her golden mangalasutra on the pretext of the design of the said chain being nicely crafted, the accused No.1 has stolen the said golden mangalasutra and ran away from the said shop and thereafter handed over the said mangalasutra to accused No.2 to dispose the same, who in turn sold the said chain at Muthoot Fin Corp, thereby the accused No.2 has committed offence punishable U/s.420 & 414 of IPC.

3. On receipt of First Information Statement by the complainant/CW-1, Basaveshwaranagar Police have registered the case in Cr. No.79/2022 for the offences punishable U/s.379 & 420 of IPC and transmitted the FIR to the jurisdictional Magistrate.

After completion of investigation, the IO has filed the final report against the accused Nos.1 & 2 for having committed the offence punishable U/s.420 & 414 of IPC.
4.

In view of the instant case being split up case, the cognizance had already been taken of the offences U/s.420 & 414 of IPC, in original C.C. No.5206/2023 (renumbered as C.C. No.588/2025)
5.
The accused No.2 appeared through her counsel and filed bail application.
The same was considered and she has been enlarged on bail.

6. After appearance of accused No.2, charge sheet copy, statement of the witnesses and documents along with the charge sheet has been supplied to the accused No.2 in compliance of Sec.207 of Basaveshwaranagra Police Station vs Vaitegi Alias Amul on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122948548/

sentences.text: P.C. Thereafter, this court has heard the learned Sr. APP and the counsel for accused No.2 and framed charge by reading over and explaining the allegations of the prosecution to the accused No.2 for the offences punishable U/s.420 & 414 of IPC.
The accused No.2 has not pleaded guilty and claimed to be tried.
7. The prosecution has examined one witness as PW-1 and got marked five documents as Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-5 and closed its side of evidence.

The statement of the accused No.1 as contemplated U/s.313 of Cr.P.C., is dispensed as there is no any incriminating materials appearing against her and submitted that she has no any defence evidence on her behalf.
8. Heard both the sides.
Perused final report, oral and documentary evidence adduced by the prosecution.

9. On the basis of the above, the following points arise for consideration of this court viz.,
1) Whether prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubts that, on 21.05.2022, at about 12-15 pm., while CW-1/PW-1 was at her Dry Fruits Shop, situated at No.222, 7th Cross, 1st Main,
Manjunathnagar 3rd Phase, the accused No.1, having stolen her golden mangalasutra, handed over the same to accused No.2, who in turn sold the same at Muthoot Fin Corp despite her knowledge regarding the said mangalasutra being stolen by accused No.1 and assisted to dispose the said managalasura to deceive PW-1 and thereby accused No.2 committed an offences punishable U/s.414 & 420 of IPC?
2) What order?
10.

On the basis of the oral and documentary evidence, the findings of this court to the above point is as under:
 Point No.1 : In the Negative  Point No.2 : As per final order  for the following  REASONS 11. Point No.1: The prosecution burdened to prove the guilt of the accused persons beyond all reasonable doubts has got examined one witness as PW-1 and got marked five documents as Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-5.
12.

It is the prosecution's case that, on 21.05.2022, at 12-15 pm., while CW-1/PW-1 was at her Dry Fruits Shop, situated at No.222, 7th Cross, 1st Main, Manjunathnagar 1st Phase, the accused No.1 having drawn the attention of PW-1 by requesting PW-1 to pack Dry Fruits weighing half KG each,

3 same, who in turn sold the said chain at Muthoot Fin Corp, thereby the accused No.2 has committed offence punishable U/s.420 & 414 of IPC.
13.
CW-1, who is cited as victim/complainant is examined as PW-1 and she has accounted as to having lodged the FIS at Basaveshwaranagara PS in connection to the theft of her mangalasutra.
She has also accounted as to having affixed her signature on the document styled as spot mahazar at the request of police officials.
The said FIS and spot mahazar are marked as Ex.P-1 and Ex.P-2 and signatures are marked as Ex.P-1(a) and Ex.P-2(a) respectively.
Further, she has accounted regarding her golden mangalasutra being traced and handed over to her on 24.06.2022.
The property released panchanama bearing signature of the witness is marked as Ex.P-3 and her signature is marked as Ex.P-3(a).
She has pleaded ignorance regarding the contents of Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-3 so also the signatories to the Ex.P-2 & Ex.P-3.
She has failed to identify the accused No.2 before the court and also denied regarding statements being given by her to the police officials in connection to the case on hand.

14. PW-1 is treated as hostile witness and permitted to be cross-examined by the learned Sr. APP,
the endeavor on her part to elicit the prosecution's case as per the FIS and spot mahazar so also prosecution papers by confronting their contents to PW-1 so also the accused No.1 in person has turned futile exercise.
The specific suggestions as to the accused No.2 has been confronted to her by the police officials on 07.06.2022 has been denied by the witness.

The denied portion in the voluntary statements of the PW-1 insofar as the weight of golden mangalasutra dated 22.05.2022 as well as confrontation of accused No.2 at police station on 07.06.2022 are marked as Ex.P-4 and Ex.P-5 respectively.
15. As the victim/complainant has deposed contrary to the prosecution papers, the prayer of learned Sr. APP for issuance of witness summons to other prosecution witnesses has been rejected.

16. An anxious examination of prosecution papers, evidence on record and arguments canvassed by the learned Sr. APP and the counsel for the accused No.2, this court has to examine the prosecution's allegations as to the CW-1's golden mangalasutra weighing 36 grams being stolen by accused No.1 by distracting her attention with an ulterior intention to deceive PW-1 and the said chain being handed over to accused No.2 to dispose for making unlawful gain.

17. It is pertinent to note that, the testimony of victim/complainant, who has deposed contrary to the prosecution's case insofar as identification of accused No.2 is crucial aspect which goes to the root of the matter.

Furthermore, the testimony of said PW-1 in having not given the statement in connection to confrontation of accused No.2 by the Investigating Officer on 07.06.2022, cannot be considered to appreciate the prosecution's claim put-forth in the case on hand.

That apart, the involvement of accused No.2 in the case on hand is unable to be gathered, as the PW-1 has very much denied the identification of accused No.2, which is a crucial aspect as per Ex.P-5.
18.

It is also pertinent to note that, the prosecution's case is unable to be gathered as the charge sheet except the statement of CW-10, who is the Branch Manager of Muthoot Fin Corp as well as seizure panchanama, no any document to show the managalasutra being sold by accused No.2 in the Basaveshwaranagra Police Station vs Vaitegi Alias Amul on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122948548/
4 said Fin Corp and the consideration pertaining to the said managalasutra being paid has been placed before this court, by production of necessary documents.

sentences.text: This creates a doubt in the mind of the court regarding the very involvement of accused No.2.
In absence of relevant documentary evidence pertaining to the Muthoot Fin Corp in order to incriminate the accused No.2, the criminal guilt cannot be fixed upon her.

19. That apart, the arguments of the prosecution as to accused No.2 had intention to deceive the PW-1 as such she accepted the golden managasutra from accused No.1 and sold the same at Muthoot Fin Corp in itself cannot be appreciated as the PW-1 has failed to identify regarding the involvement of accused No.2 in the case on hand, in the custody of Investigating Officer on 07.06.2022.
20.

In the case on hand, overall examination of testimony of the prosecution witness and prosecution papers, this court is justified to opine that the prosecution's case is tainted with substantial improvements, omissions and contradictions.
It is needless to point out that the very ingredients of the alleged offences are unable to be gathered from the testimony of the material prosecution witness.
This court without any hesitation holds prosecution has miserably failed to bring home guilt of the accused No.2 beyond all reasonable doubts.
Accordingly this court proceeds to answer Point No.1 in the Negative.
21. Point No.2:

In view of the above findings on point No.1, this court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER Acting under section 248(1) of Cr.P.C., the accused No.2 is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable U/s. 420 & 414 of IPC.
Consequently, accused No.2 is set at liberty.
Corresponding bail bonds and surety bond of the accused No.2 stands canceled.
Office is directed to place the entire records along-with C.C. No.588/2025.
